gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the same 600 W ALLPOWERS SP039 panel is sold in three kits whose batteries hold 45%, 84% and 100% of one day's output from it (1,024 / 1,920 / 3,168 Wh against about 2,295 Wh), or that the cheapest of them is $718.20 and ships now.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), OutageReady, and Dealectric's own under-$3,000 (cited) and panels-included pages. StormWatts already has the method (usable W = smaller of panel W and station solar cap; sun-hours = Wh / (W x 0.85); Wh per day = W x 4.5 x 0.85, capped at the battery) for 24 kits, but no ALLPOWERS or ABOK kit; its only rows with 600 W or more are the EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4 + 640 W and the BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2x 500 W. OutageReady has no kit with 600 W of panels. Dealectric's under-$3,000 page already gives the R3500 + SP039 at 5.3 h and $0.55 per Wh, so that one row is not new. The P1800 + SP039, R2500 V2 + SP039 and Apex 300 + 3x 200 W rows, and the share of a day's output each battery can store, appear on none of them.
decides: Among kits with 600 W of panels that ship now, the R3500 + SP039 ($1,753.93 link, $0.55 per Wh) is the only one whose battery can store a full day from its panel (2,295 Wh into 3,168 Wh), which confirms it as the pick. The P1800 + SP039 ($718.20 link) is the cheapest 600 W kit and also ships now, but its 1,024 Wh battery fills in about 2 sun-hours and can store only about 45% of the day's output, so it suits shoppers who run loads while the sun is up. The R2500 V2 + SP039 ($1,080.69 link, $0.56 per Wh, stores 84% of the day) is the middle option for a shopper who can wait for the Dec 11, 2026 dispatch. The BLUETTI Apex 300 + 3x 200 W costs $0.82 per Wh and dispatches in late January 2027, so it loses on both price and date.
